topics.label: Introduction to the Complement System
topics.groupedBecause: This opening framing introduces the lecture topic, contextualizes its complexity, and sets expectations for the session.

topics.label: Fundamentals, Nomenclature, and Central Role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational principles of the complement cascade, explain its naming conventions, and highlight the central biochemical role of C3.

topics.label: Complement Activation Pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three distinct biochemical pathways that detect pathogens and converge on activating surface-bound complement.

topics.label: Complement Effector Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream processes through which activated complement coordinates pathogen elimination and immune recruitment.

topics.label: Regulation of Complement and Host Cell Protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses how host regulatory proteins prevent unintended complement activation and membrane damage on self tissue.

topics.label: Clinical Consequences of Complement Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how deficiencies in specific complement components result in distinct clinical disease presentations and infection susceptibilities.

topics.label: Pathogen Evasion Strategies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the evolutionary adaptations used by microbes to circumvent complement-mediated destruction and their practical applications.

topics.label: Closing Remarks and Preview of Next Lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This closing framing concludes the lecture on complement and previews the upcoming session on the adaptive immune system.
